subject: general
question: The former Chief Justice of India, Ranjan Gogoi, was preceded by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dipak Misra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Justice Dipak Misra served as the 45th Chief Justice of India (CJI).
 
• He was appointed as the Chief Justice of India on 28th August 2017.
 
• Justice Dipak Misra succeeded Justice J. S. Khehar.
 
• He retired on 2nd October 2018 and was succeeded by Justice Ranjan Gogoi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Justice of India (CJI)**

 
 
• The Chief Justice of India (CJI) is the head of the judiciary system in India and the Supreme Court of India.
 
• The CJI is appointed by the President of India based on seniority.
 
• The CJI is responsible for the allocation of cases and appointment of constitutional benches which deal with important matters of law.
 
• The first Chief Justice of India was Justice Harilal J. Kania.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court of India**
 
 
• The Supreme Court is the highest judicial court in India.
 
• It was established on 28th January 1950 and is located in New Delhi.
 
• The Supreme Court functions primarily as an appellate court, dealing with appeals against judgments from lower courts.
 
• It also has original jurisdiction over certain cases such as disputes between states or between the union and states, and issues related to the enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Appointments**
 
 
• Judicial appointments in India are governed by a collegium system, where the CJI and a forum of four senior-most judges of the Supreme Court recommend appointments and transfers of judges.
 
• The President of India appoints judges based on these recommendations.
 
• This system aims to maintain the independence of the judiciary.
